newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Wednesday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt higher on continued light hog receipts, which forced packers to aggressively compete for inventories, dealers and packer buyers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold at prices fully steady with Tuesday's, but could turn higher as the day progressed. Hogs at country stations sold at $56.50 to $57.00 and hogs delivered to the plant sold mostly at $57.50 to $58.00, with a few at $59.00, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $57.00 to $58.00 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 per cwt higher at $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants, sources in that area said.
"There's not a lot of hogs moving yet, but demand sure is strong," one Indiana dealer said.
Ohio hogs sold $0.50 higher at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.50 at plants.
Hog prices also were supported by firm pork prices Tuesday, sources said.
Fresh loins on Tuesday were quoted generally steady, butts were up $2-$4 per cwt and belly prices advanced $2-$3, USDA said in the central U.S. carlot pork report.
There were 74.25 loads of pork and 19.5 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold, USDA reported.
